title: Payment service slow responses
executive_summary: Payment-service p99 latency rose from ~300ms to ~1.7s mean (peak 3.6s) starting ~18:09-18:10Z. The latency is inherited: payment-service calls to auth-service /v1/token/verify slowed first, and payment timeouts to auth-service (3000ms) followed. auth-service degraded starting ~18:07Z (p99 90ms to ~2s, error rate 0.3% to 1.5%, CPU 30% to 39%, request queue time up to 9.7s), and its logs show slow JWKS refreshes from the identity-provider starting 18:06Z. Payment's own DB, CPU, and error rate are flat, so the payment pods are not the source. The most likely cause is upstream degradation of the identity-provider/JWKS path inside auth-service, but no identity-provider telemetry is available to confirm it.

hypotheses.description: Slow identity-provider JWKS refresh (external dependency) degrades auth-service token verification, which queues requests and causes payment-service timeouts. Mechanism: Slow JWKS fetches from identity-provider (120-980ms, rising from 18:06Z) hold auth-service request threads; /v1/token/verify queue time grows (2-9.7s), auth p99 rises from ~90ms to ~2-4s and CPU climbs; payment-service calls to auth time out at 3000ms and its p99 follows about 2-3 minutes later. The causal ordering (auth onset 18:07 before payment onset 18:09-18:10) matches.

However, the change preceded the latency onset by about 35 minutes with no change in payment metrics during the gap.

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): upstream_dependency_degradation in auth-service - Slow identity-provider JWKS refresh (external dependency) degrades auth-service token verification, which queues requests and causes payment-service timeouts.
corrective_actions: Mitigate now: add tighter timeouts and a circuit breaker on payment-service calls to auth-service, and allow stale JWKS keys to be served in auth-service during IdP slowness
Investigate the identity-provider/JWKS latency path and confirm with IdP health data
Revert the payment-service log.level DEBUG change (OPS-2898) if still active
preventive_actions: Increase JWKS cache TTL and use background refresh with stale-while-revalidate in auth-service
Add bulkhead and queue limits for /v1/token/verify
Add timeouts and a circuit breaker around all auth calls from payment-service (per HIST-2025-031)
monitoring_recommendations: Dashboard for identity-provider latency and error rate, and auth-service JWKS refresh duration
Alert on payment-to-auth timeout rate above 1%
Alert on auth-service queue time and thread-pool saturation
limitations: Telemetry covers only T0-60m to T0+30m, so the pre-17:35 baseline is limited
Correlation of onset times (auth 18:07Z, payment 18:09Z) is consistent with causation but is not proof

conclusion: Payment-service latency is a downstream symptom of auth-service degradation, which started about 18:07Z alongside slow identity-provider JWKS refreshes. Payment pods, payment DB, and postgres are healthy. The most probable root cause is upstream identity-provider/JWKS slowness, but this is unconfirmed because identity-provider telemetry is absent and the auth CPU increase is unexplained.
